plan.summary:
Links now store their folder in a new `folder_id` column, so the folder view needs no join.

- A migration adds the column and an index.
- `move_link` writes `folder_id` and sets `dirty`.
- The `Link` proto message gains a `folder_id` field.
- A comment in an older migration is reworded.
plan.riskRationale: This change adds a schema column and a public proto field. Existing rows will have a NULL folder_id, and the evidence shows no backfill. The write path change is small.
plan.storyArc: The change adds a stored folder reference to links. First the schema gets the column and index. Then the write path fills it. Last, the proto exposes it to clients.

noise.reason: Comment-only rewording in an old migration. No runtime effect.

topics.title: Add folder_id column and index to links
topics.narrativeBrief: What schema change lets links remember their folder? Check the nullable column, the index, and that no backfill exists for old rows.

topics.title: Write folder_id when a link moves
dependsOn: Add folder_id column and index to links
topics.narrativeBrief: How does move_link keep the cached folder current? Verify the UPDATE sets folder_id and dirty together, and that other write paths such as link creation are not covered here.

topics.title: Expose folder_id on the Link proto message
dependsOn: Add folder_id column and index to links
topics.narrativeBrief: What contract change do clients see? Verify the new field 3 is additive, and that an empty string means the root folder.
